//: THE VERIFIED TIER of the Mochiii MCP marketplace: servers someone writing code in the editor would use --
files, git, GitHub, databases, a browser, docs -- not connectors to SaaS accounts. Each entry was chosen by
a person and is pinned here, in full, by a person: the package, its exact version (an OCI image by its
digest, since a tag can be moved), the arguments after it, and the variables it reads. `npm run mcp:sync`
does NOT move these pins; it only rebuilds the community tier and says when the registry has a newer
version of a verified server. A bump is an edit to this file, then `npm run mcp:handshake`, which starts
the new pin and records its tools/list -- the build refuses a verified entry with no passing record.
`namespace` is the server's name in the official MCP Registry, where the registry lists it; the MCP
project's own reference servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory, sequential-thinking) are not there.
`env` lists variables by NAME only: Mochiii passes them through, never stores a value in a catalog.
`cwd: workspace` starts the server in the project; without it a server gets a private folder of its own.
Filesystem, git and fetch overlap Mochiii's own confined tools. They were left out until 2026-10-26 and
are offered now because people ask for them by name; the add flow still makes the user acknowledge that
the server runs unconfined, and filesystem and git start in the project only. postgres and sqlite are Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases: the MCP project's
own postgres server is deprecated on npm and had a read-only bypass, and its sqlite server is archived.

servers.name: Filesystem
servers.description: Read, write, move and search files in the open project, from the MCP reference servers. Reaches only the project folder it starts in.

servers.name: Git
servers.description: Status, diff, log, branches and commits in the project's Git repository, from the MCP reference servers.

servers.name: GitHub
servers.description: GitHub's official server: repositories, issues, pull requests, code search and Actions, through your own token.

env.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A GitHub personal access token. Scope it to what you want Mochiii to reach.

servers.name: PostgreSQL
servers.description: Run SQL against a PostgreSQL database and inspect its schema, tables and indexes. Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases, with its prebuilt PostgreSQL tools.

env.name: POSTGRES_USER
env.description: The user to connect as. A read-only role is the safe choice.

servers.name: SQLite
servers.description: Query a SQLite database file and inspect its tables. Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases, with its prebuilt SQLite tools, started in the project.

env.name: SQLITE_DATABASE
env.description: Path to the database file, relative to the project or absolute.

servers.name: Playwright
servers.description: Drive a real browser with Playwright: navigate, click, fill forms and read pages through the accessibility tree.

servers.name: Chrome DevTools
servers.description: Inspect and debug a live Chrome: network requests, console, performance traces and DOM, from the Chrome DevTools team.

servers.name: Fetch
servers.description: Fetch a web page or API response and hand it to the model as Markdown, from the MCP reference servers. It can reach any URL your machine can, local ones included.

servers.name: Context7
servers.description: Up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples for libraries, pulled into the model's context on request.

env.name: CONTEXT7_API_KEY
env.description: A Context7 API key, for higher rate limits. It works without one.

servers.name: ESLint
servers.description: Lint files in the project with its own ESLint configuration and explain the problems found. The ESLint team's official server.

servers.name: Next.js DevTools
servers.description: Next.js documentation, upgrade guides and a running dev server's errors and routes, from the Next.js team.

servers.name: Nx
servers.description: Understand an Nx monorepo: its projects, their dependencies, targets and generators, and the Nx docs. From the Nx team.

servers.name: MongoDB
servers.description: Query and manage a MongoDB database: collections, documents, indexes and aggregations. MongoDB's official server.

env.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING
env.description: The connection string of the database to work with. Without it, the model has to be given one with the connect tool.

env.name: MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY
env.description: Set to true to allow only reads.

servers.name: Redis
servers.description: Read, write and search data in Redis, from Redis's official server. Connects to localhost:6379 unless told otherwise.

env.name: REDIS_HOST
env.description: The Redis host, if not localhost.

env.name: REDIS_USERNAME
env.description: The user to connect as, if any.

servers.name: Terraform
servers.description: Terraform Registry providers, modules and policies, for writing accurate Terraform, and HCP Terraform workspaces with a token. Runs Terraform operations only if you enable them yourself.

env.name: TFE_TOKEN
env.description: An HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise token, for workspace tools. Registry lookups work without it.

env.name: TFE_ADDRESS
env.description: Your Terraform Enterprise URL, if you do not use HCP Terraform.

servers.name: Memory
servers.description: A persistent knowledge graph the model can write to and recall from across conversations: decisions, conventions, what a module is for. An MCP reference server.

env.name: MEMORY_FILE_PATH
env.description: Where to keep the knowledge graph. Set it, or the graph may not outlive a package cache clean.

servers.name: Sequential Thinking
servers.description: A structured tool for step-by-step problem solving that can revise and branch its own reasoning. An MCP reference server.
